hints.title: Stone Reduction Divisibility Criterion
hints.text: Every merge combines exactly k piles into one, removing k - 1 piles net. Reaching a single pile is possible if and only if n - 1 is evenly divisible by k - 1.

hints.title: Step Partitioning Invariant
hints.text: When partitioning a range [i, j], split points m must advance by increments of k - 1 so that the left sub-interval reduces to a single valid stone pile.

hints.title: Prefix Sum Augmented Range Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Precalculate prefix sums for stone weights. Maintain a table dp[i][j]. For lengths from k to n, find the minimal split cost across m stepping by k - 1. Whenever the current window length minus one is divisible by k - 1, add the sum of all stones in range [i, j]. Return dp[0][n - 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^3) time and O(N^2) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all merge permutations has exponential branching that exceeds standard time limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval DP uses O(n^2) space and O(n^3 / k) time by stepping through valid pile-reducing partitions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must identify the arithmetic condition (n - 1) % (k - 1) == 0 and optimize subproblem splits by step size k - 1.
